9.title: Washington, the SEC & Crypto's Regulatory Split
9.summary: Congress is still stalled, but regulators are preparing to move anyway. Reporting this morning says SEC Chair Paul Atkins and CFTC Chair Michael Selig are preparing crypto-focused initiatives while the Senate market-structure effort remains stuck. The SEC is expected to consider a tailored offering regime for certain crypto investment contracts at an August 15 open meeting. At the same time, BRICS nations are discussing ways to connect fast-payment systems and central bank digital currencies. The theme for this hour is simple: crypto policy is not waiting on one giant bill. Different regulators and different countries are building their own rails in parallel.
9.tweet: 9 AM on Silver Bull Radio: Congress is stalled, but the regulators are not. The SEC is preparing tailored crypto offering rules while BRICS countries discuss linking payment systems and CBDCs. Crypto policy is getting built from multiple directions at once.

stories.headline: SEC and CFTC prepare crypto-focused plans while Senate legislation stalls
stories.context: Reporting says Wall Street regulators are preparing major crypto initiatives even as the Senate market-structure process remains delayed.
stories.talking_point: Does regulatory action from agencies reduce the urgency for Congress, or create even more need for a single market-structure law?

stories.headline: SEC to consider tailored offering rules for certain crypto investment contracts
stories.context: The SEC is expected to consider whether to propose a more tailored offering regime for certain crypto-related investment contracts at its August 15 open meeting.
stories.talking_point: Would a tailored offering path actually unlock more legitimate U.S. crypto issuance, or just create another compliance layer?

stories.headline: CLARITY Act remains stalled as regulators prepare to move
stories.context: The broader federal market-structure bill remains unresolved while regulators prepare initiatives that could shape the industry before Congress acts.
stories.talking_point: Which matters more for builders right now: a comprehensive law or workable agency-level rules they can actually use?

stories.headline: BRICS countries discuss linking fast-payment systems and CBDCs
stories.context: BRICS members are discussing potential links between their payment systems and central bank digital currencies, according to India's central-bank leadership.
stories.talking_point: If cross-border payment blocs become more interconnected, what does that mean for dollar stablecoins and private blockchain payment rails?

stories.headline: The U.S. regulatory path and global digital-money path are diverging
stories.context: The U.S. debate is focused heavily on private crypto markets and restrictions around a retail CBDC, while other countries continue exploring state-backed digital payment infrastructure.
stories.talking_point: Are private stablecoins becoming the U.S. answer to CBDCs whether policymakers call them that or not?

10.title: Bitcoin Range, ETF Demand & Institutional OTC
10.summary: Bitcoin is still trapped in a narrow range, with reporting putting the market roughly between sixty-two and sixty-six thousand dollars. ETF buying is helping support demand, but miners and other sellers continue offsetting those inflows. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs brought in about eight hundred fifty-four million dollars last week, their strongest haul since April, although Wintermute says it wants to see sustained flows before turning fully bullish. The institutional story goes deeper than ETFs: Wintermute says institutions accounted for seventy-two percent of its spot OTC volume in the first half of 2026. That is a strong signal that professional crypto liquidity is getting deeper even while price goes sideways.
10.tweet: 10 AM on Silver Bull Radio: BTC is stuck around the $62K-$66K range, spot ETFs pulled in about $854M last week, and Wintermute says institutions drove 72% of its spot OTC volume in H1. Price is quiet. Institutional plumbing is not.

stories.headline: Bitcoin remains stuck in roughly a $62,000 to $66,000 range
stories.context: ETF demand is being offset by selling pressure from miners and other holders, keeping Bitcoin range-bound ahead of additional macro catalysts.
stories.talking_point: When price stays flat while regulated demand keeps coming in, who is absorbing whom — buyers or sellers?

stories.headline: Spot Bitcoin ETFs bring in about $854 million in their strongest week since April
stories.context: Bitcoin ETF demand improved sharply last week, but Wintermute cautioned that one strong stretch is not enough to declare a durable trend.
stories.talking_point: How many weeks of sustained ETF demand would actually change the structure of this market?

stories.headline: Institutions drove 72% of Wintermute spot OTC volume in the first half of 2026
stories.context: Wintermute says institutional clients made up nearly three quarters of its spot over-the-counter volume, pointing to deeper professional liquidity in Bitcoin and Ethereum markets.
stories.talking_point: Is OTC volume a better institutional-adoption signal than ETF headlines because it captures activity we do not see on public exchanges?

stories.headline: Metaplanet moves 3,881 Bitcoin between internal wallets
stories.context: Blockchain data showed the Japanese treasury company moved Bitcoin between wallets it controls rather than to an exchange, meaning the transfer was not identified as a sale.
stories.talking_point: How often does large on-chain movement get misread as selling simply because the market sees coins move?

stories.headline: Bitcoin miners continue exploring AI infrastructure economics
stories.context: Mining companies including Riot are increasingly being discussed through the lens of AI and data-center economics rather than Bitcoin mining alone.
stories.talking_point: If miners can earn more from AI compute, what happens to Bitcoin hash power, mining economics and the long-term security budget?

11.title: Tokenized Stocks: Growth, Settlement & the Reality Check
11.summary: Tokenized equities are one of the strongest stories on the board today. Reporting puts tokenized stocks at about two-point-four-nine billion dollars in value, roughly six hundred percent higher than a year ago. Crypto.com is rolling out tokenized stock derivatives, KuCoin is integrating Ondo tokenized assets, and Robinhood Chain is already seeing decentralized-exchange liquidity form around tokenized equities. At the same time, a GSR executive is warning that tokenization hype has moved faster than real platform usage on some heavily restricted, walled-garden systems. That gives us the right question for this hour: is tokenization actually scaling, or are we still confusing product launches with real liquidity and real settlement activity?
11.tweet: 11 AM on Silver Bull Radio: tokenized stocks are around $2.49B and up roughly 600% in a year. Crypto exchanges are racing into equities and settlement is shrinking toward seconds — but GSR is warning that some tokenization platforms still have almost no real usage. Time to separate adoption from hype.

stories.headline: Tokenized stocks reach about $2.49 billion, up roughly 600% in a year
stories.context: Tokenized equity products have expanded rapidly as crypto exchanges and blockchain firms push deeper into traditional-market exposure.
stories.talking_point: Is six hundred percent growth proof of product-market fit, or simply what happens when a tiny market gets its first real wave of distribution?

stories.headline: Crypto.com rolls out tokenized stock derivatives
stories.context: Crypto.com is joining the race to offer blockchain-based equity exposure, although the products provide price exposure rather than traditional shareholder ownership rights.
stories.talking_point: Does it matter to users whether they own the underlying share, or just a token that tracks the price?

stories.headline: Tokenized equities are shrinking settlement from a business day toward seconds
stories.context: The tokenization thesis increasingly centers on faster settlement compared with the traditional next-business-day securities process.
stories.talking_point: If settlement can happen in seconds, which existing pieces of market infrastructure become unnecessary or radically smaller?

stories.headline: Robinhood Chain tokenized-stock liquidity concentrates heavily in Uniswap
stories.context: Reporting says Uniswap has captured the overwhelming majority of decentralized liquidity around tokenized stocks on Robinhood Chain, with more than ninety tokenized stocks and ETFs available around launch.
stories.talking_point: Does decentralized liquidity become a feature of regulated securities markets, or will regulators push that activity back into permissioned venues?

stories.headline: GSR executive warns tokenization hype is outrunning actual platform usage
stories.context: A GSR executive argues that some highly restricted tokenization platforms remain walled gardens with weak trading volume despite strong industry narratives.
stories.talking_point: What metric should we use to judge real tokenization adoption: assets issued, trading volume, settlement volume, active wallets or capital efficiency?

stories.headline: BlackRock expands tokenized money-market products as banks race toward blockchain markets
stories.context: BlackRock is reported to have introduced two tokenized money-market products this month as major financial institutions continue expanding tokenized-market infrastructure.
stories.talking_point: Do tokenized cash products matter more than tokenized stocks because cash is the settlement layer everything else needs?

12.title: RWA Collateral, Stablecoin Payments & On-chain Capital
12.summary: The final hour is about capital actually operating on-chain. The broader real-world-asset market is being measured at more than seven hundred thirty billion dollars when stablecoins are included, pushing the conversation from tokenized representation toward collateral and capital efficiency. Stablecoin card spending has reportedly moved above seven hundred fifty million dollars, showing how digital dollars can reach consumers through familiar payment infrastructure even when merchants ultimately receive local currency. Galaxy and Sharplink are launching a one-hundred-twenty-five-million-dollar fund designed to put institutional Ethereum to work in on-chain opportunities, while tokenized Treasury products continue expanding. This is where the pieces meet: stablecoins, collateral, yield, tokenized funds and programmable settlement.
12.tweet: 12 PM on Silver Bull Radio: RWAs are becoming collateral, stablecoin card spending has topped $750M, Galaxy + Sharplink are launching a $125M institutional ETH fund, and tokenized Treasury products keep expanding. The story is shifting from assets being on-chain to capital actually working on-chain.

stories.headline: Real-world assets move from tokenization toward collateral
stories.context: Coverage puts the wider tokenized RWA landscape above seven hundred thirty billion dollars when stablecoins are included and frames collateral utility as the next important primitive.
stories.talking_point: Is collateral use the point where tokenized assets stop being digital wrappers and become genuinely new financial infrastructure?

stories.headline: Crypto card spending tops $750 million as stablecoin payments grow
stories.context: Stablecoins are increasingly reaching consumers through card infrastructure, with tokens often converted into local currency at the point of sale so merchants can use familiar payment systems.
stories.talking_point: Do stablecoins need consumers to know they are using stablecoins, or is invisible infrastructure actually the winning model?

stories.headline: Payoneer CEO says the stablecoin battle is won at the last mile
stories.context: Payoneer's leadership argues that converting stablecoins into usable local currency remains one of the most important practical challenges in global payments.
stories.talking_point: Is the real stablecoin moat issuance, distribution, compliance, local off-ramps or merchant acceptance?

stories.headline: Galaxy and Sharplink launch $125 million fund to deploy institutional ETH on-chain
stories.context: The new fund is designed to put institutional Ethereum capital into decentralized-finance and other on-chain opportunities rather than simply holding the asset passively.
stories.talking_point: Does institutional ETH adoption ultimately depend more on productive yield and collateral use than on price appreciation?

stories.headline: Anchored launches tokenized funds connecting assets, liquidity, compliance and settlement
stories.context: Anchored is launching institutional alternative strategies through programmable infrastructure designed to connect traditional-finance assets with on-chain distribution and settlement.
stories.talking_point: Is the winning RWA platform the one with the best tokenization technology, or the one that best connects compliance, liquidity and distribution?

stories.headline: Franklin Templeton continues expanding tokenized U.S. Treasury exposure
stories.context: Franklin Templeton is highlighted as a leader in tokenized U.S. Treasury bills, with reported year-to-date growth of roughly one-point-six billion dollars.
stories.talking_point: Why have Treasuries become the cleanest institutional bridge between traditional finance and on-chain markets?

stories.headline: Grayscale argues AI creates new demand for verifiable blockchain infrastructure
stories.context: Grayscale's research argues that AI agents increase demand for verifiable records, identity and payment infrastructure that public blockchains such as Ethereum and Solana can provide.
stories.talking_point: Could AI agents become a bigger blockchain adoption driver than human crypto users over the next cycle?
